source_review: Whole authenticated tagged Material 16.2.14 modules prove that all three legacy names originally alias public input/testing classes. Complete minimum Material 21.2.14 and 22.1.7 modules execute through genuine public CDK testing and Angular Core namespaces; TestElement/LocatorFactory remain controlled protocols.

Twenty-six of twenty-nine class method bodies match the tag after token normalization. The three changed bodies are input.with, input.isDisabled and native-select.with. Stable public declarations and strict complete declaration-closure consumers were checked individually; no private or deprecated product dependency is added.

The current input parent can report false for native disabled=true when the attribute is the literal false, and true for an enabled native input with aria-disabled=true. The owned testing adapter restores the tagged native-property reader, and its factory constructs the owned class. Placeholder/data-placeholder fallback already matches the tag and is retained.

The owned testing adapter retains the public current-parent subtype, host selector, inherited getters and focus/value behavior. Constructor identity differs from the former public reexport; strict constructor and instance assignability remain valid. This narrowly scoped testing change implements the user-delegated conservative TypeScript allowance without component forking.

The optional current input/native-select label filters are additive and use the stable public getLabel contract. Positive/negative/regex label protocol cases pass. Actual legacy mat-label markup is covered by two newly added native Angular regressions, whose artifact-bound execution is still pending.

Native select and option algorithms, host selectors, getters, option filters, single/multiple selection and empty selection error match the tag. Five mutations reject parent-behavior fallback, parent-constructor leakage and silently ignored value/placeholder/label predicates.
